I found two behaviour changes in the refactor and fixed both. I also put back one module path the file split had removed. The rest of the diff is behaviour-neutral: quote and semicolon style, arrow functions, renamed locals, JSDoc examples and the new import paths. I compared the tax, exchange-rate and discount-code tables with `main` and they are identical.

1. **Unknown discount codes stopped being rejected** (`src/discount.js`). On `main`, `applyDiscountCode(5000, 'NOPE')` throws `unknown code: NOPE`. The refactor folded that check into `if (!code || !entry) return 0`, so a mistyped code quietly gave no discount instead of an error. It throws again now.
2. **Zero quantity became valid** (`src/lineItems.js`). The new `assertInt` helper was called with a minimum of `0` for `qty`, but `main` requires `qty >= 1`. A line item with `qty: 0` now fails again with `bad qty for <sku>`.
3. **`require('./src/money')` stopped working.** Splitting `money.js` into `money/round.js` and `money/format.js` removed that import path. I added `src/money/index.js`, which re-exports `roundCents`, `sumCents` and `formatMoney`, so old imports still resolve and the split stays.

I added one test for each of the first two fixes. Both tests fail when I undo the fixes, and the full suite now passes (519/519). The existing tests missed these because none of them used an unknown code or a quantity of zero.

The changes are not committed yet; tell me if you want them committed.
